def-conditional-subgaussian-increments:
## Definition

Assume the Axiom of Choice (AC) [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the conditional-expectation existence convention. Let
$(\Omega,\mathcal F,(\mathcal F_t)_{t\in\mathbb N_0},P)$ be a discrete filtered probability space
[[def-filtration-and-filtered-probability-space]], and let $(X_t)_{t\ge1}$ be a real-valued adapted process
[[def-adapted-and-integrable-stochastic-process]]. Fix $\mu\in\mathbb R$ and a proxy $\sigma^2>0$.
The increments are **conditionally sub-Gaussian around $\mu$ with proxy $\sigma^2$** when, for every
integer $t\ge1$ and every fixed $\lambda\in\mathbb R$, $e^{\lambda(X_t-\mu)}$ is integrable and
$$
\mathbb E_P[e^{\lambda(X_t-\mu)}\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]\le e^{\lambda^2\sigma^2/2}\quad P\text{-almost surely},
$$
where conditional expectation means the class of integrable versions of
[[def-conditional-expectation-as-an-ae-class]] represented as in
[[def-conditional-expectation-given-a-sigma-algebra]]. The exceptional null set may depend on $t$ and
$\lambda$; no common null set over the uncountable set $\mathbb R$ is assumed.

The integrability of $X_t$ follows from the two cases $\lambda=1$ and $\lambda=-1$: conditional
expectation preserves the integral, so both $e^{X_t-\mu}$ and $e^{-(X_t-\mu)}$ have finite expectation,
and $|X_t-\mu|\le e^{X_t-\mu}+e^{-(X_t-\mu)}$. The proxy is an upper bound in the conditional
moment-generating-function inequality; it is not asserted to be a variance. Independence and identical
distribution of the increments are not part of this definition.
def-gaussian-mixture-confidence-sequence:
## Definition

Let $\sigma^2>0$ be a supplied scale, let $\rho>0$ be a tuning parameter, and let $\alpha\in(0,1)$.
For $v\ge0$ define
$$u_\alpha(v):=\sqrt{(v+\rho)\log\!\left(\frac{v+\rho}{\alpha^2\rho}\right)}.$$
The expression is real because $(v+\rho)/(\alpha^2\rho)>1$. For a real data sequence
$x_1,x_2,\ldots$, set $\bar x_t=t^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^t x_i$ and define
$$C_0:=\mathbb R,\qquad C_t:=\left[\bar x_t-\frac{u_\alpha(t\sigma^2)}{t},\,\bar x_t+\frac{u_\alpha(t\sigma^2)}{t}\right]\quad(t\ge1).$$
The endpoints are included. This definition specifies an interval rule only; it makes no coverage or
time-uniform validity assertion.
lem-gaussian-exponential-mixture-integra:
## Statement

Assume AC. For $\rho>0$, $v\ge0$, and $s\in\mathbb R$, let
$\pi_\rho=N(0,1/\rho)$ under the normal-law convention of
[[def-standard-normal-and-normal-laws]]. Then
$$\int_{\mathbb R}\exp\!\left(\lambda s-\frac{v\lambda^2}{2}\right)\,\pi_\rho(d\lambda)=\sqrt{\frac{\rho}{v+\rho}}\exp\!\left(\frac{s^2}{2(v+\rho)}\right).$$
lem-conditional-subgaussian-exponential-:
## Statement

Assume AC and let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,(\mathcal F_t)_{t\in\mathbb N_0},P)$, $(X_t)_{t\ge1}$, $\mu\in\mathbb R$, and $\sigma^2>0$ satisfy
[[def-conditional-subgaussian-increments]]. For each fixed $\lambda\in\mathbb R$, set
$$S_0(\mu):=0,\qquad S_t(\mu):=\sum_{i=1}^t(X_i-\mu),\qquad L_t^\lambda(\mu):=\exp\!\left(\lambda S_t(\mu)-\frac{\lambda^2t\sigma^2}{2}\right).$$
Then $(L_t^\lambda(\mu))_{t\ge0}$ is a nonnegative test supermartingale for the singleton null family $\{P\}$, with $L_0^\lambda(\mu)=1$.
lem-gaussian-mixture-boundary-crossing-e:
## Statement

Let $\alpha\in(0,1)$, $\rho>0$, $v\ge0$, and $s\in\mathbb R$. Define
$$M(v,s):=\sqrt{\frac{\rho}{v+\rho}}\exp\!\left(\frac{s^2}{2(v+\rho)}\right).$$
For $u_\alpha$ from [[def-gaussian-mixture-confidence-sequence-boundary]],
$$M(v,s)\ge\frac1\alpha\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad |s|\ge u_\alpha(v).$$
thm-gaussian-mixture-test-supermartingal:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,(\mathcal F_t)_{t\in\mathbb N_0},P)$ and $(X_t)_{t\ge1}$ satisfy
[[def-conditional-subgaussian-increments]] for $\mu\in\mathbb R$ with known proxy $\sigma^2>0$.
Fix $\rho>0$. Define $S_0(\mu)=0$, $S_t(\mu)=\sum_{i=1}^t(X_i-\mu)$, $V_t=t\sigma^2$, and
$$M_t(\mu):=\sqrt{\frac{\rho}{V_t+\rho}}\exp\!\left(\frac{S_t(\mu)^2}{2(V_t+\rho)}\right)\quad(t\in\mathbb N_0).$$
Then $M(\mu)$ is a nonnegative test supermartingale for $\{P\}$, with $M_0(\mu)=1$.
thm-subgaussian-mixture-confidence-seque:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R$, let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,(\mathcal F_t)_{t\in\mathbb N_0})$ be a common discrete filtered measurable space, and let $(P_\theta)_{\theta\in\Theta}$ be a family of probability laws on it. Let $(X_t)_{t\ge1}$ be a common real-valued process that is adapted under each $P_\theta$, and suppose that for every $\theta\in\Theta$ its increments are conditionally sub-Gaussian around $\theta$ with the same known proxy $\sigma^2>0$ under $P_\theta$ in the sense of
[[def-conditional-subgaussian-increments]]. Fix $\rho>0$ and $\alpha\in(0,1)$. For $t\ge1$, set
$$\bar X_t:=\frac1t\sum_{i=1}^tX_i,\qquad C_t:=\Theta\cap\left[\bar X_t-\frac{u_\alpha(t\sigma^2)}{t},\,\bar X_t+\frac{u_\alpha(t\sigma^2)}{t}\right],$$
where $u_\alpha$ is from [[def-gaussian-mixture-confidence-sequence-boundary]], and set $C_0:=\Theta$. Then $(C_t)_{t\ge0}$ is a $(1-\alpha)$ confidence sequence for $\theta$:
$$P_\theta\bigl(\theta\in C_t\text{ for every }t\ge0\bigr)\ge1-\alpha\quad(\theta\in\Theta).$$
The claim is pointwise in $\theta$ and requires no measurable structure on $\Theta$, independence, or identical distribution of the observations.
